C-SAFETY-REVIEW-LANES.Name: Per-lane safety review locks: a long non-local review must not block every other commit
C-SAFETY-REVIEW-LANES.ApprovalBasis: Owner instruction 2026-10-27 (translated from Russian): «их два — локальный и удалённый» — there are two reviewers, local and remote — followed by «делай» after the proposal to split the single inference lock by lane so a long non-local review no longer serializes the whole repository.
C-SAFETY-REVIEW-LANES.Summary: review() currently takes one exclusive fcntl.flock on .git/mark-safety/inference.lock for the whole operation: candidate creation, deterministic scan, Gitleaks, the two owner-local model passes and the independent non-local pass. The two reviewers are different resources (a local Ollama model with one loaded-model slot and a remote Ollama endpoint), and the deterministic scan already uses a per-process TemporaryDirectory, so the global lock over-serializes. Measured on the C-TITLEBAR-MODE-CHIPS commit (2026-10-27): 123 local chunks completed, the non-local phase reached chunk 10 after ~18 minutes, and every other commit in the repository received "Another repository safety review owns the inference slot" throughout. This change replaces the single lock with a short candidate lock around snapshot/scan/final identity and two named lane locks: one around local_review and one around non_local_review. Each lane stays single-flight, a waiting commit can finish its local phase while another commit is remote-bound, and candidate identity, receipts and the human override keep their current semantics.

Problem.Description: One repository-wide lock guards two independent resources. A large candidate (123 chunks for the titlebar change) holds it through every remote model call, so no other commit or push can be reviewed for hours; the failure message does not say which resource is busy. The local and non-local reviewers are separate endpoints, and the deterministic scan is already concurrency-safe, so the serialization is broader than the invariants require.
Problem.RootCauseTimestamp: 2026-10-27 07:08–07:28 +0500, titlebar commit PID 77637: local_review chunks 1–123 then non_local_review chunks 1–10+ while inference.lock stayed held.

Goals.R-1: Replace the single inference.lock with named locks: candidate.lock for the short snapshot, scan and final identity/receipt section; local.lock around local_review; non-local.lock around non_local_review. No code path may acquire all three for the duration of a model review.
Goals.R-2: Keep each lane single-flight: at most one local review (one loaded local model slot) and at most one non-local review at a time. A local phase may run while another operation is in its non-local phase.
Goals.R-3: Preserve candidate integrity: the candidate snapshot, deterministic checks, Gitleaks, final identity recheck and private receipt stay exact. A concurrent commit that changes the candidate identity invalidates the older review, which must fail closed and re-stage.
Goals.R-4: Make contention observable: a blocked operation names the busy lane (local or non-local), and no new bypass, environment variable or override path is introduced.
Goals.R-5: Prove the split: tests show local proceeds while non-local is held, two local reviews serialize, two non-local reviews serialize, and concurrent reviews cannot corrupt per-candidate debug evidence. Update docs/commit-push-safety.md and M-064/V-M-064.

P1.Title: Lock split in tools/security_gate.py plus per-candidate review evidence

P2.Title: Concurrency regressions, docs, graph and verification deltas

C-SAFETY-REVIEW-LANES.Dependencies: The current two-reviewer gate (C-SAFETY-GATE-MODEL-REVIEW) is on main; its reviewer configuration, ownership preflight, chunking and override semantics are unchanged by this change.

Constraints.Constraint: The local endpoint must never run two reviews concurrently; reviewer_ownership and the one-loaded-model assumption stay authoritative inside local.lock.
The non-local lane remains single-flight by default; this change does not add remote concurrency.
Candidate creation, deterministic scan and the final identity check stay serialized in candidate.lock, so two staged candidates cannot interleave their scan or receipt writes.
last-model-review.json is shared today; it must become per-candidate (identity in the filename) and be written atomically, or two overlapping reviews corrupt it.
Lock files stay owner-only (0600) in the private safety directory; flock releases them when a process dies, so no stale-lock cleanup command is added.
The explicit MARK_SAFETY_OVERRIDE path, prompts, models, chunk size, phases and receipt schema for completed reviews are unchanged except the debug-evidence filename.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Running chunks of one review in parallel, or running two local reviews at once.
Changing reviewer endpoints, models, prompts, chunking, verdict schema or the human override.
Making the non-local lane concurrent beyond one in-flight review.
Changing push lanes, history-rewrite lanes or screenshot binary policy.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: review() acquires candidate.lock for snapshot/scan and the final identity/receipt section, local.lock around local_review, and non-local.lock around non_local_review; no inference.lock remains and no lock is held across both model lanes.

With non-local.lock held by one operation, a second operation completes local_review; a third local operation fails closed on local.lock with the lane message; two non-local operations fail closed the same way.
The contention error names the lane (for example "owns the local review slot" / "owns the non-local review slot").
Per-candidate debug evidence is written atomically and two overlapping reviews leave two intact files.
npm run safety:test passes; grace lint --path . --assertions current reports zero errors; docs/commit-push-safety.md, M-064 and V-M-064 describe the two lanes.

VerificationIntent.Verification: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests/security -p 'test_*.py' (npm run safety:test) — existing review, override, reviewer-ownership and push-lane cases stay green plus the new lane-concurrency cases.

A targeted concurrency test: patch local_review/non_local_review to block on events, run two review() calls, and assert the second local phase completes while the first is inside non_local_review; assert two local phases do not overlap.
grace lint --path . --assertions current and grace status --path . --with modules --json — zero errors before handoff.
Manual observation on the next large commit: a concurrent small commit completes its local phase while the large one is in non-local, and the blocked message names the lane.
